summary: The first algebraic branch of the saturated de Rham–Witt construction: Dieudonné complexes, the décalage description of Frobenius, Verschiebung, saturation, the Cartier criterion and the finite-level completion tower. This does not yet identify the construction with crystalline cohomology.

nodes.title: Dieudonné complexes
nodes.statement: A Dieudonné complex is a cochain complex of abelian groups (M*,d) with a map of graded abelian groups F:M*→M* satisfying dF(x)=pF(dx); morphisms commute with d and F. For a p-torsion-free complex, (η_p M)^n={x∈p^nM^n : dx∈p^{n+1}M^{n+1}} is a subcomplex of M*[p^{-1}] (Construction 2.1.3; for complexes in nonnegative degrees η_pM⊆M, footnote 1). For termwise p-torsion-free M, a Dieudonné structure F is equivalent to a map of cochain complexes α_F:M*→(η_pM)*, α_F(x)=p^nF(x) for x∈M^n, with inverse F(x)=p^{-n}α(x).
hypotheses: p is a prime, fixed throughout the source (BLM lines 237 and 463: 'a prime p which is implicitly fixed throughout the sequel').
Termwise p-torsion-freeness is required for the equivalence with the décalage description, not for the definition of a Dieudonné complex.
proofSteps: Use dF=pFd to check that p^nF lands in the η_p submodule and commutes with the differentials.
Conversely divide α(x) by p^n inside the localization; membership in η_p makes the result an element of M.
Check the two constructions are inverse and preserve morphisms.
acceptance: Distinguish F, a graded map, from α_F, a chain map.
Check the source equation dF=pFd on a homogeneous element and under tensor products.

sources.locator: Definition 2.1.1, Construction 2.1.3 and Remark 2.1.4, pp.13–14; extracted lines 517–549
sources.match: The source constructs both maps with their degree scaling.

nodes.title: Saturated Frobenius
nodes.statement: A Dieudonné complex is saturated when it is termwise p-torsion-free and F:M^n→{x∈M^n:dx∈pM^{n+1}} is bijective in every degree. Equivalently, α_F:M→η_p M is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: A Dieudonné complex; saturation includes p-torsion-freeness.
proofSteps: Identify p^n times the target of F with (η_p M)^n.
Use the established α_F dictionary to transport bijectivity to a chain isomorphism.
acceptance: Check saturation is preserved by isomorphism of Dieudonné complexes.
Do not replace a strict chain isomorphism here with a derived fixed-point assertion.

sources.locator: Definition 2.2.1 and Remark 2.2.2, p.14; extracted lines 555–565
sources.match: The definition and its equivalent décalage formulation appear consecutively.

nodes.title: Verschiebung and the differential
nodes.statement: On a saturated Dieudonné complex define V uniquely by F(Vx)=px. It is injective and satisfies FV=VF=p, FdV=d and Vd=p dV.
hypotheses: The complex is saturated; in particular F is injective and M is p-torsion-free.
proofSteps: Since d(px) belongs to pM, saturation puts px in the image of F; injectivity gives existence and uniqueness of V.
FV=p implies injectivity of V. Precompose with F and cancel F to obtain VF=p.
Combine dF=pFd and FV=p, cancel p, and then postcompose with V to obtain the differential identities.
acceptance: Check all identities as maps of graded groups; V itself generally does not commute with d.
Retain the cancellation hypotheses in every step.

sources.locator: Remark 2.2.3 and Proposition 2.2.4 with proof, p.14; extracted lines 566–581
sources.match: The proof uses injectivity and p-torsion-freeness for the stated cancellations.

nodes.title: Iterated Frobenius divisibility
nodes.statement: For a saturated Dieudonné complex and every r≥0, F^r identifies M^n with {x∈M^n:dx∈p^rM^{n+1}}. Consequently every cocycle belongs to the image of every iterate F^r.
proofSteps: The forward inclusion follows from dF^r=p^rF^rd.
For dx=p^r y with r>0, p-torsion-freeness gives dy=0.
Write x=F(x′) and y=F(y′) by saturation, cancel pF to obtain dx′=p^{r−1}y′, and apply induction.
acceptance: Apply the result to a cocycle to obtain infinite F-divisibility without asserting compatible choices beyond the unique lifts.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.2.5 and Remark 2.2.6, p.15; extracted lines 583–599
sources.match: The source gives this exact induction and its cocycle consequence.

nodes.title: Saturation by iterated décalage
nodes.statement: Every Dieudonné complex M* admits a saturation M*→Sat(M*): a map to a saturated complex through which every map to a saturated complex factors uniquely. First quotient by the graded subgroup T* of elements killed by a power of p; on the p-torsion-free quotient take the direct limit of the sequence M*→(η_pM)*→(η_pη_pM)*→⋯ whose transition maps are α_F, η_p(α_F), η_p(η_p(α_F)),… (display (8)). Saturation is left adjoint to the inclusion DC_sat↪DC.
hypotheses: A Dieudonné complex; no initial saturation or p-torsion-freeness assumption.
proofSteps: Reduce to the p-torsion-free case by replacing M* by M*/T*; the source states this reduction without detail (p.15, lines 613–615). The elementary checks behind it are that T* is stable under d and F, that M*/T* is p-torsion-free, and that every map to a saturated (hence p-torsion-free) complex kills T*.
On the torsion-free quotient construct the η_p iteration.
Use commutation of η_p with filtered colimits to make the induced α_F invertible on the colimit.

The source asserts that the direct limit 'is a saturation of M*' (line 621) without further detail; the universal property is the check that a map to a saturated target extends uniquely at each η_p stage and that the compatible colimit map is unique.
acceptance: Prove existence and uniqueness of the universal factorization.
Do not infer that M→Sat(M) is a quasi-isomorphism for an arbitrary singular input.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.3.1 and Corollary 2.3.2, p.15; extracted lines 600–623
sources.match: The proof constructs the saturation from the torsion quotient and displayed colimit.

nodes.title: Cartier criterion for saturation
nodes.statement: If M is a termwise p-torsion-free Dieudonné complex and F induces an isomorphism of graded groups M/p→H*(M/p), then M/p→Sat(M)/p is a quasi-isomorphism.
hypotheses: M has Cartier type as defined in BLM 2.4.1; saturation alone does not imply this hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the generic Bockstein comparison (η_pM)/p≃(H*(M/p),β).
A map that is a quasi-isomorphism modulo p stays so after η_p: it induces an isomorphism on the Bockstein complexes.
Factor the Cartier map through α_F:M/p→(η_pM)/p; the Bockstein comparison and two-out-of-three make α_F a quasi-isomorphism.
Apply η_p repeatedly and pass to the filtered colimit describing saturation.
Passing from the stages (η_p^k M)/p to Sat(M)/p uses that cohomology and reduction modulo p commute with filtered colimits; this is not stated in the source.
acceptance: Verify the triangle with F and the Bockstein comparison commutes.
Keep Cartier type separate from saturation; the source warns the saturation itself is generally not Cartier type.

sources.locator: Definition 2.4.1, Proposition 2.4.5, Corollary 2.4.6 and proof of Theorem 2.4.2, pp.16–18; extracted lines 661–764
sources.match: The proof reduces the full saturation tower to the first map using the Bockstein comparison.

nodes.title: The de Rham–Witt completion tower
nodes.statement: For saturated M* form W_r(M)*=M*/(im V^r+im dV^r) for r≥0 (W_0(M)*=0), the restriction maps Res:W_{r+1}(M)*→W_r(M)*, and the completion W(M)*=lim_r W_r(M)*. F descends to F:W_r(M)*→W_{r−1}(M)* and V to V:W_r(M)*→W_{r+1}(M)*; passing to the limit makes W(M)* a Dieudonné complex, the construction is functorial, and the tautological map ρ_M:M*→W(M)* is a map of Dieudonné complexes (Remark 2.5.3).
hypotheses: M is saturated; r≥0 and W_0(M)=0.
proofSteps: The denominator is a subcomplex because d²=0.
Use FdV=d and FV=p to show F lowers the level.
Use Vd=p dV to show V raises the level.
Pass the compatible graded maps and the differential to the inverse limit; check naturality under maps of saturated complexes.
acceptance: Check the indexing of F, V and restriction on finite quotients.
Keep proof of saturation/strictness of the completion and comparison with classical de Rham–Witt as further results.

gaps.title: Strict completion and crystalline realization
gaps.detail: The finite-level completion tower was read through Remark 2.5.3. Later proofs that completion is saturated/strict, and comparison with classical and crystalline cohomology, remain outside the inspected range.

gaps.title: Typed comparison with existing Witt operators
gaps.detail: Mathlib WittVector/Frobenius.lean and Verschiebung.lean are relevant existing ring-level carriers. Review R2 grep of the TauCeti project found no Dieudonné-complex, saturation or de Rham–Witt construction (its 'Dieudonné' hits are the Cartan–Dieudonné theorem on quadratic forms). A saturated complex has different degree-sensitive operators; their exact Lean integration has not been checked and no implemented status is claimed.

gaps.title: Elementary facts asserted without proof in BLM §§2.1–2.5
gaps.detail: The source states without proof: that α_F is a map of cochain complexes (Remark 2.1.4); that η_p commutes with filtered colimits (Proposition 2.3.1 proof, line 616); the reduction to the p-torsion-free quotient M*/T* and that the displayed colimit 'is a saturation' (lines 613–621); that im(V^r)+im(dV^r) is a subcomplex (Construction 2.5.1); and, in the proof of Theorem 2.4.2, that the colimit description of Sat(M*) reduces the mod-p quasi-isomorphism to the stages. Each is an elementary check recorded in the node proof steps; none has been discharged elsewhere.
